title: App not working and team doesn’t reply
body: App is very confusing to me, I don’t get the whole progression stuff and tbh and the dark theme is very jarring. Good logging but not worth the membership..

title: App Won’t Open
body:
I was enthusiastically using this app with every workout. Paid for a full years membership and suddenly it stopped working. It doesn’t open on my IOS. All updates have been made and still nothing. 
So buyer beware. It’s got good qualities but pretty useless if I don’t have access to it. I’ll be asking for my money back.

title: Best out there + suggestions
body:
I have used push for over a year and loved it! I took a break and then used other apps thinking there might be better ones out there but I was wrong. PUSH is really the best out there. Better pricing especially for what you get I love Joe Delaneys videos and so stoked about it app. Forget testing out other apps like me this is real the best out there! Joe Delaney is my hero!  


My suggestions. 

It would be cool to be able to put eliminate exercises that I don’t want to do like deadlift or back squat out of the program instead of having to swap the exercises all the time. Those exercises hurt my back.( my technique could be bad tho). Also it would be cool to have like a de load week as part of the program. Maybe you have that and I don’t see it though.

title: Love this app but…
body: Love this app! Genuinely the best app I’ve used for the gym, and have felt myself get stronger the more workouts I do with it. At times it can feel a bit repetitive, but it does switch it up. More importantly; what I feel it still really needs is a travel mode when you don’t have access to weights, so that you can maintain muscle growth progress or maintenance even when you do not have access to the gym.

title: The Watch App Makes This 5 Stars
body:
App is great for tracking and the auto progression takes the stress out of progressive overload

But the watch app takes it over the top. So convenient.

title: Consistently sore from my workouts
body:
Love this app, it’s a perfect app in progress! Please add ability to save when adding exercises to a workout plan. 

I know it auto saves in some cases. But it’s unclear when it does that. So a manual button would be helpful.

title: Great App
body: Would love if you guys could implement this into the Apple Watch it’s one of the best training apps out there.

title: Almost perfect
body:
Great app!! However would love to be able to select which specific pieces of gym equipment are available when using a limited gym/limited dumbbell weights. Also would love a widget for home screen showing the progress body as a daily reminder which muscle groups need focus/rest. 

Big ask, but would like this to sync to whoop for muscular load data. No idea if this is even possible without whoop’s coordination tho lol

title: Excellent
body: I’ve tried and paid for many other apps to log and track workouts, and this one just clicks. You’ve earned a subscriber and I highly recommend this to anyone including both people who are experienced for just getting started. The only thing I think this app needs is support for live activities.

title: Love It
body: App is great, easy to use, looks nice, has easy volume trackers per muscle group, and the dev team is responsive and makes consistent updates

title: It’s good
body: I’ve used multiple workout apps, this one is particular special because it tracks how many times you hit each muscle group and I’ve always had difficulty doing that, I just want to see this app more adaptive and easier to access maybe make the RPE easier to access however drop sets and myo sets are a very good touch. Back to being more adaptive I would like for it to not just go up 5 pounds I find myself having to change that a lot overall a very good workout app for the price point. But please make these changes

title: Great App but missing Apple Watch support
body: Agreed with all the other reviews, I’ve really been enjoying this app. But it desperately needs an Apple Watch App to complete the experience. This creates a 3/5 star experience for me.

title: Apple Watch support
body: I gave it 4 stars it’s pretty good used it a full two years I am now 56 and actually building new muscle, is it just the app no but while everyone in the gym doing random exercises I follow the program . So far almost 2026 and still no Apple Watch support, also Be mindful of lifting as it sometimes suggests the progressive increase can take you beyond your limits adjust it accordingly or switch to maintain muscle.

title: Glitchy AF
body: Could be a great app. Let me know when the bugs get worked out. For now, pen and paper is still easier than dealing with all the glitches and random in-app behavior.

title: Best Workout App By Far!
body:
I have been training for 15+ years and have tried over a dozen apps and workout programs/trackers. 

This one is the best hands down. Joe Delaney is my hero.

title: Awesome
body: I’ve used several similar apps. This one is the best.

title: Live Activities Please
body: Simple, high quality app. The addition of live activities would bring it to five stars.

title: It’s ok, has potential
body: So far I do like the simplicity of this app, and how it tracks workouts. The only problem I’m having is when it creates a program for me, I select I only have dumbbells. But when I started the workouts, it was giving me all these exercises for machines (that you’d find in a gym). I thought I had accidentally selected that as an option, so I deleted my current program and created a new one, careful to only select dumbbells. But again, it’s suggests mostly machine workouts. I can manually change them to something else, but I spend more time trying to find a replacement workout than I do actually working out. Hopefully over time it’ll realize I only have dumbbells, but for now I have to change it every time. Not sure if it’s a bug or something, but I committed to the yearly and will likely not renew.

title: No well rounded programs
body: There is no deload and progression. Not well rounded

title: Stuck on loading screen
body: Would love to try this app but am stuck on the loading screen. Recently updated to 18.6.2

title: App stopped working :(
body:
Had a login error, tried to login again and it just keeps pushing back to login screen. I’m subscribed with my apple account. There was an update but now it just crashes. I tried to reach developer support but the webpage is not found and the contact page on the app website never sends the message. Big bummer because i loved using the app. Hope it’s fixed real
soon.

UPDATE: after d*cking around a good while, i just signed up again directly with my apple account email address and it thankfully restored my sub. So all good again. Though i had to recreate my profile. Bumping up to 4 stars. Otherwise, as far as workouts go, it’s 5 stars for me as a novice. hyper practical and straight forward.

title: Hard crash on open
body: After latest update. Hard crash on open :(

title: Love this app (small request)
body: Love this app. It takes so much guesswork out of workout plans. It does however, lack apple watch functionality which can be really frustrating. If I want my lift to be tracked on my watch I have to start a separate workout on apple health and it’s pretty inconvenient. Please add watch functionality and it’ll be perfect!

title: Good but boring/unmotivating
body: It’s a good workout tracker but their “ai” doesn’t really do much. It adds 5lbs to every workout even if you plateau. It’s supposed to change the exercise after you plateau, but the app hasn’t changed any of my exercises after 1.5 month of plateauing. It’s the same exercises week after week. Gets boring after a while.

title: Blown away
body: I've been using this app for the past 4-5 months or so, and have added weight on all the lifts in my plan. The automatic progressive overload makes working out and gaining frictionless. However, I am incredibly impressed with their customer support. I reported a bug relating to RIR within the app and there was an update pushed out within 48 hours resolving the issue. 10/10 could not recommend more.

title: Great app but not a fit for my needs
body: Very well designed app that I considered to keep using, but the exercises available weren’t right for my training style. 1. The auto generated workout option requires you to have some weights or machinery, making body weight plans impossible. My training style is kettlebell + calisthenics. 2. Calisthenic exercises and progressions are generally not included in the app. It would be possible for me to add all those manually but do not think it would be worth the subscription cost. If you add in a way to do bodyweight/calisthenic training in the app with some more customizability to the auto-generated program I would happily pay!

title: Great, No Frills Required
body:
Since my last review they incorporated the “keep screen awake” function, which I missed.
Would still be good to have to way to incorporate cardio training…or have it read your Apple fitness activity and incorporate the data into training/recovery plans.

title: Buggy, bad support
body: The app bugged out on me by Day 3 with it, tried contacting support and the page for support is buggy too.  Don’t pay for this

title: Best workout app ever
body: This is the most simple, science backed, accurate, and easy to use workout app I’ve ever used. 1000% recommend. The information it provides tracks with my kinesiology degrees and work experience in the fitness & health field. Yet, you don’t need to know any of this, just follow the workouts it gives you and you will see progress quickly.

title: Not quite there yet
body: It’s a very well designed with some excellent auto progression and generated programs to follow. That said, it makes the mistake so many apps do. It does not easily present you a graph of progress per lift. It’s great to see the volume im doing per exercise but that is secondary to the most important thing of all which is “am I getting stronger?”

title: App crashing
body: Been using this app for years, lately the app won’t open at all, immediately crashes

title: App crashes.
body: The app crashes the moment I start an exercise. When it use to work it worked very well. I have an iPhone 16 pro. I reported the issue and have gotten no response. Disappointing to say the least.

title: Great App
body: Love the app. I’ve tried many apps and this app has exactly what I was looking for. Something that’s going to push me to do better while hitting all of the different muscle groups. The only thing I wish is that I could control the app from my Apple Watch.

title: AMAZING
body: I am doing exercises I never thought to consider in my workout routine and it feels amazing !!

title: Finally a good workout app
body:
For the last year or so I’ve signed up for at least ten different apps to get a good workout plan. Been super frustrated with each one for various reasons — too expensive, too confusing to use, not practical, etc.

This app is phenomenal. It tells me when to increase weight (progression) and the overall design and functionality of the app is perfect. It’s simple and has everything you need.

Highly suggest trying it out. You shouldn’t have to pay $25-$60 per month for a workout app. This is by far my favorite lifting app.

title: Easy to use.
body: Makes working out much simpler. Easy to use. Makes lifting brainless for a Dad of 3.

title: No place to report bugs?
body: Since there’s no clear way to report bugs..when creating a custom routine and you go to add an exercise..if you have to create the exercise from there, once created and added the routine duplicates every exercise in that routine

title: Good but few bugs
body:
I like the interface and exercise choices are pretty good focusing on compound movements with a few accessory lifts. 

There is a bug when replacing an exercise that reverts it back to kg from lbs but seemingly puts a random number in the weight column. Then when you try to switch, it says “switch to kg” even though it’s already in kg. Then you have to switch again to lbs and it converts the random weight that was there to lbs and seemingly doesn’t have the weight that was used in the prior workout. 

The warmups are kinda goofy with ridiculously light weights to start like 5lbs on a barbell squat for the first warmup set. It also defaults the number of reps for the warmup to the same number as working sets. I think it would be better to have first warmup set as light weight with ~12 reps then slightly heavier at 8 reps, then closer to working weight at 4 reps before going to working sets. Could also be fixed by letting the user adjust the weight and reps of warmup sets.

Also there are 2 exercises for barbell deadlift but none for dumbbell deadlift.

title: Buggy
body:
I’m currently in a one year subscription. I think the price is fine but, right now I won’t resubscribe. The app has potential but is buggy and I’m concerned there’s too much reliance on AI. Hopefully the AI part is more marketing than reality.

The Good: I like the choice of exercises and the variations in sets/reps. I like how muscle groups are prioritized throughout the week.

The Bad: The app always recommends increasing weight by 5lbs regardless of whether I’m deadlifting 200lbs or doing side laterals with 20lb dumbbells. Once I fail to complete the days sets/reps, the algorithm fails miserably. The new recommended weight sometimes resets back to 5lbs or, in one case, went negative.

title: Guy
body: App just crashes. Don’t waste your time. It doesn’t even open.

title: HELP
body: Downloaded 5-6 updates since the re-work and still can’t get the app passed the startup screen. iOS is up to date too. Still my favorite app of all time but let’s go, fix this. Thanks

title: Close to perfect
body:
Really good workout design, nice UI, good customization but there are few more places they could add fine tuning (ideally without overwhelming the novices). 

Joe if you read these, my one request is to allow customization of the timer notification sound. On the Strong app it was a bell sound not shared with any of my other apps, but in Push it sounds just like the notification noise for Instagram, Reddit, Hinge, etc., leading to false positives where I have to look at the phone to confirm it’s the set timer. Also would be nice to be able to manually start a timer like in Strong.

Otherwise, looking forward to future updates given how far this app has come in a short time.

title: Great Update
body:
Update was definitely worth the wait, barely got it today. 

Love the new aesthetic, but also love the intuitive nature of the app. At first I was unsure but once I actually started playing around with it it was a no brainer that this update is a better version of the app. A feature from this update I REALLY enjoyed was the automatic exercise change for exercises that haven’t progressed. I was confused as to why I had barbell squats in my leg day today, but I thought honestly about how my leg press hasn’t progressed much, and the change in pace made for such a solid leg day. And I hate leg days. Also love the multi-program & superset features been waiting a min for those.

I just think a home page that actually feels like a home page would be nice to see in future updates, maybe like a feature that shows you how many weeks into your current program you are or something above the body part graphic. Or even the old version with your name and “it’s a great day to lift” but that’s not really important to the functionality, and as an app it does everything else you could want. 

I’m also going to be honest, I wouldn’t have paid for the last version if I hadn’t forgotten to cancel my 7 day trial. This time around, definitely seems worth renewing, especially if the watch version is close. It’s a tiny bit inconvenient to have to grab my phone so often when it’s the last thing I want on my mind. Still 5 stars without that, because although there’s potential it is everything it says so. And compared to similar apps I’ve tried like ‘Strong’ or this one is just way nicer and has flow

title: Quality
body: Been using Joe Ds stuff since before apps and this new update is a great QOL change. Only bad point is that I keep thinking the notifications are from Uber.

title: Best workout app
body: Tried this since it came out. One of the most straightforward and simple app I’ve used to the point it’s worth paying for IMO if your going to pay for a workout app

title: Love it but v3 won't open at all.
body: This app is just (was just) so cool. Been loving it since downloading it. A joy to use, so slick and intuitive. Some minor improvements had crossed my mind along the way but overall, the best out there. Then came v3 which just hangs and won't open and that's that. I'm sure this is a normal update growing pain and I look forward to it being resolved but for now, for the new year, it's a bummer! That said, still giving 5 stars because I know these things happen and honestly this app is just the best of what's out there.

I never really write reviews but after using push almost since its infancy I’ve recently been more consistent with it for about 4-5 months. Truly has been visually the most muscle I’ve built. Feels good to get automatic updates and changes . Makes it easy. I look forward to working out :D

title: Needs a watch companion app
body: This app would be great, but it needs a Strong-like Apple Watch companion app. Super annoying having to reach for my phone every set.

title: Really does push me!
body: I love what this app has done for me. I’ve lifted before but I realize now that I hadn’t been pushing myself enough. With this app, I am getting stronger faster and without having to think about how to progress. THANK YOU! A soon-to-be grandma.

title: 50 yr old male… best program on market
body: Incredibly easy and effective. Really enjoy the change up of exercises, and the ease of altering exercises when in need of certain unavailable equipment. Notifications to stay on schedule for specific muscle groups is crucial to my workouts. Seriously cannot give this enough stars. Absolutely injected new life into my workout routines.
